The current codebase was originally designed as a simple 2D browser game. As the project grows, introducing new gameplay systems, visual effects, and eventually a 2.5D or 3D presentation becomes increasingly difficult due to tight coupling between simulation, rendering, input handling, and UI logic.

This issue proposes a major refactor aimed at modernizing the architecture, improving maintainability, and creating a solid foundation for future visual upgrades.

Goals
Separate game simulation from rendering.

Improve code organization and maintainability.

Make gameplay systems renderer-agnostic.

Enable future migration to:

Enhanced 2D visuals
2.5D rendering
Full 3D rendering (Three.js/Babylon.js)
Reduce complexity of game.js.

Improve testability and extensibility.

Proposed Architecture
Current
game.js
 ├─ Game logic
 ├─ Rendering
 ├─ Input
 ├─ UI updates
 ├─ Enemy AI
 ├─ Weapons
 ├─ Collision detection
 └─ Progression systems
Target
src/
├── core/
│   ├── Game.js
│   ├── GameLoop.js
│   └── EventBus.js
│
├── simulation/
│   ├── PlayerSystem.js
│   ├── EnemySystem.js
│   ├── WeaponSystem.js
│   ├── ProjectileSystem.js
│   ├── CollisionSystem.js
│   └── WaveSystem.js
│
├── rendering/
│   ├── Renderer2D.js
│   ├── Renderer25D.js
│   ├── Camera.js
│   └── Effects.js
│
├── input/
│   ├── KeyboardInput.js
│   ├── MouseInput.js
│   └── TouchInput.js
│
├── ui/
│   ├── HUD.js
│   ├── ShopUI.js
│   └── Menus.js
│
└── data/
    ├── weapons.js
    ├── enemies.js
    └── upgrades.js
Refactor Milestones
Phase 1: Core Cleanup

Split game.js into logical modules.

Introduce a central game state.

Create clear update/render separation.

Remove rendering dependencies from gameplay logic.

Standardize entity definitions.
Phase 2: Entity Model Improvements
Introduce a generic entity structure:

{
  id,
  type,
  position: { x, y, z },
  velocity,
  health,
  state,
  components
}
Tasks:


Add support for optional z coordinate.

Create reusable entity utilities.

Centralize entity lifecycle management.
Phase 3: Rendering Layer
Create a dedicated renderer abstraction.

Example:

renderer.render(gameState);
Tasks:


Move all canvas drawing code into renderer modules.

Add camera abstraction.

Support depth sorting.

Support future sprite billboards.

Support world-to-screen projection.
Phase 4: 2.5D Foundation
Prepare the game for pseudo-3D rendering.

Tasks:


Add height/elevation support.

Implement shadow rendering.

Implement depth-based sorting.

Prototype isometric or perspective projection.

Add simple camera movement and zoom.
Phase 5: Future 3D Compatibility
Not part of this issue's implementation, but should be enabled by the refactor.

Potential future stack:

Three.js
Babylon.js
Requirements:

Gameplay logic remains unchanged.
Rendering backend can be swapped.
World state remains renderer-independent.
Expected Benefits
Developer Experience
Easier debugging
Easier feature development
Cleaner architecture
Better scalability
Gameplay
More advanced visual effects
Better animation systems
Dynamic camera support
Easier addition of new enemy and weapon types
Long-Term Vision
This refactor lays the foundation for evolving Stranded Horizons from a simple 2D browser game into a visually richer experience while preserving the existing gameplay systems.

Priority
High

This should be completed before introducing major new visual systems or attempting a 2.5D/3D migration.</text>
